ai_extraction_prompt.content:
You are a FIX protocol specialist with deep knowledge of institutional trading. Analyze the provided exchange FIX specification and score each check_id in the rubric using a TWO-LEVEL model:

For message-level checks (check_id ends in _000):
  full_credit   = message type is explicitly documented with a tag table
  partial_credit = message is mentioned but documentation is incomplete
  no_credit     = message is absent

For tag-level checks (check_id contains a tag number):
  full_credit   = tag explicitly listed in that specific message type's table
  partial_credit = tag present but conditional, restricted, or via custom tag
  no_credit     = tag absent from that message type's documentation

IMPORTANT: Score each tag WITHIN its message type context. Tag 55 (Symbol) may be present in 35=D but not 35=F — score each separately. Do not assume a tag present in one message is present in another.

checks.description: Is NOS explicitly documented with tag tables?
Current order status at time of reject
ISO 10383 MIC code of execution venue
Fill price on partial and full executions

TradeCaptureReportAck (35=AR) is sent by the exchange to acknowledge receipt of a TradeCaptureReport (35=AE). Confirms whether the trade capture was accepted, rejected, or requires further review. Required to close the bilateral trade confirmation loop before settlement instructions.
checks.fix_reference: FIX 4.4+ message 35=AR TradeCaptureReportAck; https://fiximate.fixtrading.org/ — search TradeCaptureReportAck
checks.institutional_gap_if_missing: Without TradeCaptureReportAck, parties submitting trade capture reports cannot confirm bilateral agreement. Creates settlement break risk and breaks the end-to-end confirmation workflow required by prime brokers.
checks.tradfi_reference: FIX 4.4 35=AR; required by DTCC prime brokerage workflows; CME cleared trade confirmation

checks.description: Links the ack to the original TradeCaptureReport by match ID
checks.fix_reference: FIX 4.4+ tag 880 TrdMatchID; https://fiximate.fixtrading.org/ — search tag 880

checks.description: Status of the trade capture report: 0=Accepted, 1=Rejected, 3=Submitted, 4=Accepted with errors
checks.fix_reference: FIX 4.4+ tag 939 TrdRptStatus; https://fiximate.fixtrading.org/ — search tag 939; 0=Accepted, 1=Rejected
FIX 4.4+ tag 751 TradeReportRejectReason; https://fiximate.fixtrading.org/ — search tag 751

checks.description: Mechanism to associate on-chain wallet addresses with FIX order or trade records. The FIX-standard approach (DAWG draft) is a new PartySubIDType(803) enumeration value carrying the wallet address in the PtysSubGrp component of 35=8 or 35=AE. Alternative: custom tag or ExecID cross-reference to blockchain TxHash documented via REST. full_credit: wallet address linkage documented in FIX stream via tag 803 or documented custom tag in Parties group partial_credit: ExecID→TxHash mapping available via REST with documentation; not in FIX stream no_credit: no mechanism documented for wallet-to-trade linkage
checks.institutional_gap_if_missing: Without wallet address attribution in the FIX stream, on-chain AML screening (Chainalysis, Elliptic, TRM Labs) cannot be triggered automatically from FIX trade data. Compliance teams must manually reconcile FIX ExecIDs against blockchain transaction hashes. Tag 803 (PartySubIDType) with a wallet-specific value is the FIX Trading Community DAWG recommended approach.

scoring_logic.full_credit: Wallet address linkage in FIX via 803 or custom tag
scoring_logic.partial_credit: Linkage via REST TxHash mapping only

checks.description: Self-Match Prevention controls prevent wash trading by canceling one or both sides of an order that would match against the same firm's resting order. SMP is evaluated on 35=D (NewOrderSingle) and 35=G (OrderCancelReplaceRequest). Required for regulatory compliance with CME Rule 534, CFTC guidance, and institutional prime broker agreements.
checks.fix_reference: Coinbase Derivatives: SelfMatchPreventionID (7928) + SelfMatchPreventionStrategy (8000); https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/derivatives/fix/overview#self-match-prevention; CME Rule 534; FIX tag 7928 custom
checks.institutional_gap_if_missing: Without SMP controls, institutional clients face regulatory wash-trade exposure under CFTC and exchange rules. Prime brokers will not connect to exchanges lacking documented SMP mechanisms.

scoring_logic.full_credit: SMP documented in spec with at minimum one SMP mechanism (tag 7928 or equivalent); cancel behavior documented
scoring_logic.partial_credit: SMP mentioned but tag or cancel strategy behavior undocumented

checks.description: Identifier used to group orders for self-match prevention. Orders from the same executing firm with the same SelfMatchPreventionID will not match. Paired with SelfMatchPreventionStrategy (8000) which defines the cancel behavior.
checks.fix_reference: Custom tag 7928 SelfMatchPreventionID; custom tag 8000 SelfMatchPreventionStrategy; Coinbase Derivatives: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/derivatives/fix/overview#self-match-prevention; Kraken: tag 7928 with cancel-both/newest/oldest modes
checks.institutional_gap_if_missing: Without SelfMatchPreventionID (7928), firms cannot set order-level SMP controls. Account-level SMP only is insufficient for multi-strategy trading where different strategies within the same account may legitimately trade against each other.

scoring_logic.full_credit: Tag 7928 (SelfMatchPreventionID) documented in 35=D with cancel strategy behavior described; at least two cancel modes available (e.g. cancel-aggressor and cancel-resting)
scoring_logic.partial_credit: SMP present but only one cancel mode, or SMP is account-level only without order-level tag support
scoring_logic.no_credit: Tag 7928 absent; no order-level SMP mechanism

scoring_guide.5-7: Partial — DC available but with scope or tag gaps
scoring_guide.0-4: Not available — DC absent or critically incomplete

FIX standard tag 797 CopyMsgIndicator: https://fiximate.fixtrading.org/ (search CopyMsgIndicator or tag 797)

FINRA TRACE FIX Specification v1.5 — CopyMsgIndicator usage in regulated reporting

Configurable heartbeat interval for Drop Copy session

checks.message_name: CopyMsgIndicator — drop copy flag on FIX messages
checks.condition_note: Present only on drop copy messages; absent on order entry session messages
checks.description: FIX standard tag indicating whether a message is a copy delivered via drop copy session. Y = message is a drop copy. N = not a drop copy. FIX Trading Community recommends including tag 797=Y on all messages delivered via a drop copy session across: 35=D (NewOrderSingle), 35=G (OrderCancelReplaceRequest), 35=F (OrderCancelRequest), 35=8 (ExecutionReport), 35=9 (OrderCancelReject), 35=AE (TradeCaptureReport), 35=AR (TradeCaptureReportAck), 35=0 (Heartbeat), 35=H (OrderStatusRequest). This allows receiving systems to distinguish drop copy messages from live order entry messages without relying solely on session-level configuration.

valid_values.Y: Message is a drop copy of another message
valid_values.N: Message is not a drop copy (default; often omitted)

checks.fix_reference: FIX 4.4+ tag 797 CopyMsgIndicator; present in FIX 4.4, FIX 5.0, FIX 5.0SP1, FIX 5.0SP2, FIX 5.0SP2 EP240; https://fiximate.fixtrading.org/ (search CopyMsgIndicator); also documented in ASX 24 FIX Drop Copy Specification v2.05 and FINRA TRACE FIX Specification v1.5
checks.institutional_gap_if_missing: Without CopyMsgIndicator (797), receiving systems must rely solely on session-level DropCopyFlag or port/CompID to identify drop copy messages. Any cross-session routing or message aggregation becomes ambiguous — a compliance analytics system receiving messages from multiple sources cannot reliably distinguish DC messages from live order flow without per-message tagging.
checks.tradfi_reference: ASX 24 Drop Copy Specification: CopyMsgIndicator included in ALL drop copy messages set to Y. FINRA TRACE FIX Specification v1.5: tag 797 = Y on all drop copy messages. Both cite fiximate.fixtrading.org as the canonical tag reference.
checks.crypto_notes: Neither Kraken nor Coinbase Exchange currently documents tag 797 on their drop copy feeds. This is a gap relative to TradFi exchange implementations. Flag as partial_credit if the exchange uses a session-level flag (e.g. DropCopyFlag 9406) as functional equivalent, but note that per-message tagging is the FIX standard recommendation.

scoring_logic.full_credit: Tag 797 = Y documented on drop copy messages in the spec; applies to at minimum 35=8 (ExecutionReport) in the DC feed
scoring_logic.partial_credit: Drop copy session uses a session-level flag (e.g. custom DropCopyFlag) as functional equivalent; tag 797 not documented but DC messages are distinguishable at the session level
scoring_logic.no_credit: No mechanism documented to identify drop copy messages — neither tag 797 nor session-level equivalent

tiers.label: Market Data — buy-side price discovery & book building
tiers.description: Market data messages used by buy-side institutions for price discovery, book building, and RFQ workflows. Includes: 35=V/W/X/Y (market data subscribe/snapshot/refresh), 35=x (security list), 35=h/f (trading session status), 35=R/S/AJ/AI (RFQ workflow — request, quote, response, status report).

scoring_guide.5-7: Partial — snapshot or incremental missing key fields
scoring_guide.0-4: Not available — market data feed absent or incomplete

tiers.institutional_rationale: Buy-side institutions require FIX market data for pre-trade liquidity assessment, real-time book building for algo execution, and instrument reference data. L3 (order-level) data is significantly more valuable than L2 for execution quality analysis.

checks.description: IOI messages (35=6) are used by broker-dealers and venues to advertise buying or selling interest to institutional clients. Enables institutional buy-side firms to identify natural liquidity for large block trades without revealing full order size to the market. Supports NEW (23=N), CANCEL (23=U), and REPLACE (23=R) transaction types.
checks.fix_reference: FIX 4.0+ message 35=6 IOI; https://fiximate.fixtrading.org/ — search IOI; FIX Trading Community: Indication of Interest
checks.institutional_gap_if_missing: Without IOI support, buy-side institutions cannot receive advertised liquidity from the exchange or its connected broker network. Large block orders must rely on public market data only, increasing market impact costs.

tiers.label: Admin & Session Management — FIX connectivity foundation

scoring_guide.8-10: Production ready — full session lifecycle documented
scoring_guide.5-7: Partial — key admin messages missing or underdocumented
scoring_guide.0-4: Not ready — session management gaps are critical blockers

tiers.institutional_rationale: Reliable FIX session management is the prerequisite for all other tiers. Institutions require documented, predictable behavior for authentication, heartbeat monitoring, message recovery, and disconnect handling. An undocumented or unreliable session layer makes the exchange unusable for production regardless of its order management capabilities.

checks.field_name: Reject reason quality — tag 58 (Text) on rejects
checks.description: Tag 58 (Text) should be populated on ALL reject messages (35=3 Session Reject, 35=j Business Reject, 35=9 OrderCancelReject) with structured reject reason codes and human-readable descriptions. full_credit: tag 58 present on all reject types with machine-parseable error codes documented in spec. partial_credit: tag 58 present but generic messages only (e.g. 'rejected') no_credit: tag 58 absent from reject messages or undocumented.

scoring_logic.full_credit: Tag 58 present on all reject types; machine-parseable codes documented

checks.institutional_gap_if_missing: Without tag 58 (Text) populated on rejects, operations teams cannot determine why orders were rejected without manual exchange support escalation. In 24/7 crypto markets, this creates significant operational risk. Structured error codes in tag 58 enable automated retry logic and alerting.
checks.fix_reference: FIX 4.0+ tag 58 Text; https://fiximate.fixtrading.org/ — search tag 58; should carry structured reject reason code + human-readable description
